text:
maya: heads up, p99 on shared-gpu-pool-7 jumped ~3x around 14:03 UTC, looks like noisy tenant activity

dan: saw that, spikes line up with tenant T-392 bursts: sustained long sequences + larger batch requests :eyes:

ross: can we confirm kernel autoswitch logs? last time similar symptom was kernel flip under pressure

jin: pulled runtime logs, copying relevant snippet:
```
[14:02:58] kernel_switch: selected kernel=orex_v2 for model=resnet-llm seq_len=2048
[14:03:01] kv_cache_evict: tenant=T-392 evicted=124MB reason=slot_pressure
[14:03:02] kernel_switch: fallback_kernel=orex_v1 due_to=mem_pressure
[14:03:03] batching: flush batch_size=32 -> 8 due_to=latency_slo
```

maya: kv evictions + kernel flip in ~1s window, that smells like affinity contention (big seq tenant hitting shared slots)

anita: metrics from exporter: T-392 had concurrent streams=18, avg_seq=1800, token_rate=12/s. Other tenants ~3-5 streams.

dan: so noisy neighbor is both cache pressure and kernel mismatch. When kernel switches, latency per-token jumps since different kernel has worse vecization for long seqs

ross: is there evidence of cross-tenant batching causing mixed kernels in a single batch? that would be brutal

jin: we saw mixed batch composition in tracer: one batch included reqs with amortized seq 200 and one with 1800 -> kernel selection becomes ambiguous -> runtime chose safe kernel, dropped perf

maya: quick repro idea: throttle T-392 to 5 concurrent streams and replay similar seq distribution to see p99 delta

anita: I can mirror the workload on staging pool-2, run a controlled T-392 replay at 14:40 UTC, need ~2h for setup

dan: temporary mitigation for prod: enforce per-tenant max-ongoing-requests=8 on pool-7 and lower max_concat_seq for mixed-batch detection, that's low-risk and quick

ross: agree, also enable kv_pin for high-usage tenants (pin hot KV slots) until we finish tuning eviction policy

jin: note: kv_pin increases memory tail, need to watch OOM margins. I'll add a guard: kv_pin only if free_mem>30%

maya: can someone run perf flamegraph around the flip window? I want to see hot kernels and memcpy hotspots

anita: attaching perf excerpt from staging (abbreviated):
```
samples  cum_secs  symbol
12000   3.1       orex_v1::attention_forward
6800    1.8       memmove
4200    1.1       orex_v2::flash_attn
```

dan: memmove high — implies KV compact/evict churn. If we can reduce eviction churn, memmove will drop and orex_v2 can stay selected

ross: long term: consider tenant-aware kernel pinning (if a batch is homogeneous and matches kernel, lock kernel for that tenant affinity) + per-tenant kv_quota based on sequence profile

maya: next steps:
- anita: run staging repro and upload full perf traces (ETA 2h)
- dan: push per-tenant ongoing-requests cap to pool-7 now (rollout 5 min)
- jin: add kv_pin guard and tweak eviction threshold from 65%->75% free to be less eager
- ross: draft design doc for tenant-aware kernel affinity and quota model

anita: started replay job, logs will stream to #eng-runtime and I'll drop the trace link when done :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: applied config change on pool-7: max_ongoing_per_tenant=8 (rollout success)

maya: monitor dashboards for next 30m. If p99 doesn't fall, we'll revert and try alternative (lower batch concat threshold).

jin: minor note — lowering eviction aggressiveness may increase tail memory; I'll add an alert to autoscaler to preempt if free_mem<22%

dan: thanks team — this matches prior noisy-tenant pattern but with the extra kernel-autoswitch twist. Good call on mixed-batch detection as a mitigation

ross: if staging repro matches, we should schedule a perf regression ticket and include microbenchmarks for orex_v1 vs orex_v2 across seq lengths

maya: agreed. I'll lock a quick postmortem doc after we close the thread. For now keep updates here and @maya if you need help. :eyes:
